record.original_question: Let G be a domain in C, and H(G) the ring of functions analytic on G. It is known that, for two domains G1 and G2 , H(G1 ) is isomorphic to H(G2 ) if and only if G1 and G2 are conformally (or anticonformally) equivalent. What can be said under only the hypothesis that H(G1 ) and H(G2 ) are elementarily equivalent in the sense of model theory? For a large class of domains the corresponding problem has been solved for HC (G), the algebra of functions analytic on G, by Henson and Rubel (see [434] and [435]). (L. A. Rubel)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a domain $G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, let $H(G)$ denote the ring (under pointwise addition and multiplication) of complex-valued holomorphic functions on $G$. It is classical that for two domains $G_1, G_2 \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, the rings $H(G_1)$ and $H(G_2)$ are isomorphic (as rings) if and only if $G_1$ and $G_2$ are conformally or anticonformally equivalent.

Two rings $R_1$ and $R_2$ are said to be elementarily equivalent if they satisfy the same first-order sentences in the language of rings (i.e., $R_1 \equiv R_2$ in the sense of model theory).

Problem: Characterize, in geometric/analytic terms, those pairs of domains $G_1, G_2 \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ for which the rings $H(G_1)$ and $H(G_2)$ are elementarily equivalent. In particular, determine whether elementary equivalence of $H(G_1)$ and $H(G_2)$ implies conformal or anticonformal equivalence of $G_1$ and $G_2$, and if not, give a complete description of the elementary-equivalence classes among such rings.
artifact.category_tag: model theory of rings of analytic functions
artifact.status_search_result: A web search reveals related work by Henson and Rubel on the algebra $H_{\mathbb{C}}(G)$ of analytic functions and on rings of exponential polynomials, but no source clearly settles the elementary-equivalence classification for the ring $H(G)$ of analytic functions on arbitrary plane domains. The current status of this specific problem could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic Properties of the Ring of General Exponential Polynomials (Henson, Rubel, Singer)
status_evidence.snippet: Work by Henson and Rubel on algebraic and model-theoretic properties of rings of analytic/exponential functions, related to but not directly resolving the elementary equivalence problem for H(G).
status_evidence.claim: Related work exists by Henson and Rubel on model-theoretic properties of analytic-function algebras, but the cited literature does not provide a definitive answer for the ring H(G) of analytic functions on plane domains.
